## Introduction
R Markdown lets me write normal text while also running R code in the same document.  
When I knit it, everything updates automatically, which feels really useful for data science classes.


So far, R Markdown feels different from writing a regular report because the code and the explanation stay together.  
It makes it easier to see why I did something, not just the final answer.  
I like that the format keeps everything organized, especially because I’m building data skills and need my work to be reproducible for school and future projects.


## Math Example - LaTex
I can also add simple math using LaTeX.  
This helps when I need to show formulas or write out steps clearly.

Inline example: $\\alpha + \\beta = \\gamma$

Displayed equation:

$$
y = mx + b
$$

This is just a basic slope line equation, but it shows that R Markdown can handle math cleanly.

# R Code Chunk 1: Loading a Library and Dataset

Here is my first code chunk. I’m loading **ggplot2** and looking at the built-in `mtcars` dataset.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
head(mtcars)

summary(mtcars$mpg)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Miles Per Gallon vs Horsepower",
    x = "Horsepower",
    y = "Miles Per Gallon"
  )

```

##
Using R Markdown makes my work feel more organized and easier to follow. Everything can be a bit more organized and structured. I like that the writing and the analysis stay connected, because it helps me understand what I’m doing instead of treating the code like a separate step. This is great for any future asignment or even any projects i would have to do.
